I will keep my farm centered on the wheat-maize rotation because I have well irrigation, long experience, and enough management skill to handle a stable double-cropping system. I do not want to spread labor too thin, especially since some family members work off-farm, so I will put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, and keep a smaller block in millet because it is lower-risk, needs less water and fertilizer, and helps me diversify. On my better, easier-to-irrigate land, I will use improved or hybrid seed and push yield with moderate but not excessive fertilizer. I will keep fertilizer balanced, not only nitrogen, because after many years farming I know wheat and maize respond better when phosphorus and potassium are not neglected. I will irrigate wheat more times than the summer crops because wheat yield in my area depends heavily on water at key stages. For maize, I will rely on one good irrigation if rainfall is normal and add another only if summer is dry. Millet will stay as the more conservative crop with lower input and lower risk. I will use rotary tillage where it saves time and fits my labor situation, and I will keep pesticide use to the minimum needed to protect yield rather than spraying heavily.
